clue.text: Become depressed when left suffering

parts.note: suffering means anguish, deep pain of mind

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in their misery sinks into low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine away or lose vitality is a synonym for sinking into a low, dejected state.

clue.text: Protected against the frost but didn't hurry

definitions.meaning: insulated pipes or tanks with wrapping material to stop them freezing

explanation.definitionFit: Pipes wrapped in insulation are said to be so treated; trailing slowly behind others is the other sense of the same verb.

clue.text: Came closer to a redhead in poverty

indicators.note: the word in tells us the a and the redhead letter sit inside the word for poverty

parts.note: poverty means need, want of means
the head, or first letter, of red is R

explanation.surface: Someone drew near a ginger-haired person living in hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' is one word in the surface but splits as 'red' + 'head': its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Approached is a synonym of moving nearer to something.

clue.text: Disturb higher group

parts.note: up means higher, at a raised level
a set is a group of things belonging together

explanation.surface: Unsettle the people above us.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble or agitate someone is a synonym of disturbing them.

clue.text: Japanese warrior is imbibing a drink one knocked back

indicators.note: something knocked back is turned the other way, so the whole construction is read backwards
imbibing means drinking in, so the word is takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a common drink
a can stand for one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A Japanese fighter is downing a drink in one gulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking slang but reverses everything: IS round A RUM A gives IARUMAS, which read backwards is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the old Japanese military class of sword-bearing retainers.

clue.text: Forms with no head girls

indicators.note: having no head means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: forms are school classes, as in the fifth form

explanation.surface: School years without a headmistress, made up of girls.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a 'form' is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Young women, especially in Scottish and northern English usage, are a synonym of girls.

clue.text: Very bad actor troubled with debts

indicators.note: troubled suggests the letters of actor are thrown into disorder

parts.note: IOUs are written acknowledgments of debts

explanation.surface: A performer worried by what he owes is in a terrible state.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful or appalling is a synonym of extremely poor in quality.

clue.text: Strike-breaker promises to pay the plant

parts.note: a scab is a worker who crosses a picket line
IOUs are notes promising to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A blackleg worker's promissory notes fund the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is a flower, the field scabious.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildflower with pincushion-like blue or lilac heads, once thought to cure skin disease.

clue.text: It is more revealing to take a look along the row

parts.note: to scan is to run the eyes along something
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Peering along the seats shows skimpier outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are skimpier, with less fabric, show more of the body.

clue.text: Boys go round with me being contented

indicators.note: the word go goes round, so the boys sit inside it

parts.note: taken as written
lads means boys
taken as written

explanation.surface: Young men take a turn with me and are happy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad and cheerful is an old poetic synonym for happy or pleased.

clue.text: In time blackleg makes mistakes

indicators.note: in places the blackleg inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a strike-breaker or blackleg

explanation.surface: Eventually the strike-breaker gets things wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of errors in a printed book; the Latin plural of a slip or error.

clue.text: Cut part of the film

definitions.meaning: a short extract from a movie

explanation.definitionFit: To trim with shears, and also a short excerpt shown from a longer movie.

clue.text: Choose an examination at this college?

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Pick a spoken test at this particular university.
explanation.walkthrough: The US electoral college formally chooses the president, so 'Choose' fits the definition too; 'college' is not a university here.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of voters who choose the American president is the electoral college.

clue.text: Crack not on the suspension bridge

indicators.note: not signals that the word on is removed from the bridge's name

parts.note: the Clifton Suspension Bridge spans the Avon gorge in Bristol, England

explanation.surface: A fissure has not appeared on the famous suspended crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: CLIFTON Suspension Bridge is a landmark in Bristol, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An old variant of cleft, a split or fissure in rock.

clue.text: Politician among eleven warriors

indicators.note: among puts the politician inside the eleven

parts.note: eleven written as the figures 11 looks like two letter Is
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A member of parliament mixes with a team of fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eleven' is read visually: 11 looks like II.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zulu regiment or band of fighting men.

clue.text: Although not by the sea in Kent resort dominates

definitions.text: Although not by the sea in Kent

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters of dominates are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Kent seaside holiday town lords it over the others, though inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' suggests a seaside town but is re-sort, the anagram signal; Kent is an English county, and the answer is its inland county town.
explanation.definitionFit: The county town of Kent lies inland on the Medway, not on the coast.

clue.text: Obtain for the priest in France

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: Get something on behalf of a French cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: To get hold of or acquire is a synonym of obtaining.

clue.text: Drawn from the decks

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is made out of the letters of the decks

explanation.surface: Pulled up from the ship's floors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals that THE DECKS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlined roughly in pencil is a synonym of pictured with a pencil.

clue.text: Dirty water between Europe and Asia?

definitions.text: Dirty water between Europe and Asia?

parts.words: Dirty water between Europe and Asia?
parts.note: dirty can be described as dark or grimy, and the water between the two continents is a named inland sea north of Turkey

explanation.definitionFit: The inland sea bordered by Turkey, Ukraine and Bulgaria separates Europe from Asia.

clue.text: Rapid financial success is highly amusing

definitions.meaning: a quick big profit, as in making a fortune overnight

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden large profit on the markets, and an informal word for something hilariously funny.

clue.text: Obtain a drink outside

indicators.note: outside puts the drink around the letter a

parts.note: gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Get hold of a drink while out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire or win something is a synonym of getting it.

clue.text: Do not work with the others

explanation.definitionFit: To relax or pause from labour, and also the remaining people or things.

clue.text: Brightly-coloured American Indian?

parts.note: a dated, now offensive name for a Native American, read literally as someone whose complexion is a vivid colour

explanation.definitionFit: An old, now offensive term for a Native North American, literally one with crimson complexion.

clue.text: Got round rocky height rising in the cave

indicators.note: round says the jumbled word goes around the turned hill
rocky means unsteady, so the letters of got are shaken up
in a down clue rising means the word reads upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or height

explanation.surface: Someone climbed round a craggy hilltop inside the cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' rearranges GOT to GTO, and 'rising' turns TOR to ROT, which sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A small picturesque cavern, often artificial in a garden.

clue.text: Improves matters doesn't go on without me

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word for stopping goes around me

parts.note: ends means stops, doesn't continue

explanation.surface: Things get better, but stop when I'm absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here is the old sense 'outside', not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct and revise a text is a synonym of making it better.

clue.text: VAT, say, on nails

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, and the pronounced word is spelt differently

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is a tax

explanation.surface: Value added tax charged on ironmongery.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's value added tax, a sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sharp nails with broad heads, used for fixing carpet or fabric.

clue.text: Unseemliness of having no drink in December to start with

indicators.note: to start with puts the December phrase at the front of the answer

parts.note: O is nought, nothing
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour from going dry over Christmas month at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of propriety or decorum is a synonym of improper behaviour.

clue.text: Another girl from Alice

indicators.note: another arrangement of the letters of Alice gives a different name

explanation.surface: A second girl's name comes out of Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, such as Rosalind's cousin in As You Like It.

clue.text: Youth leader shops round about for a medicinal plant

indicators.note: the jumbled shops goes round the youth leader
about indicates the letters of shops are moved around
leader picks the first letter of youth

explanation.surface: A youth group leader goes round the shops looking for a herbal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SHOPS to HSSOP, and Y (the leader of Youth) goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic herb of the mint family, used in traditional remedies.

clue.text: Is this key found in the cupboard?

definitions.text: Is this key found in the cupboard?

parts.words: Is this key found in the cupboard?
parts.note: one kind of key opens many locks, and the same word names the dark family secret hidden in a cupboard

explanation.definitionFit: A master key opening many locks, and the secret bones in the cupboard of the idiom.

clue.text: Returning, reimbursed for the napkin

indicators.note: returning means the word for reimbursed is read backwards

parts.note: repaid means reimbursed

explanation.surface: Coming back, someone was paid back for the serviette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'napkin' is the British word for a baby's nappy; the answer is the US term.
explanation.definitionFit: The American word for a baby's nappy, from napkin in that sense.

clue.text: At home celebrated having a bad reputation

parts.note: in means at home
famous means celebrated

explanation.surface: Fêted in their own house, but notorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious is a synonym, well known for wrong reasons.
